You play as apart of the Helldivers, an elite fighting force whose aim is to quickly and decisively drop onto any planet in the galaxy and begin spreading freedom's reign upon the surface. You and your super destroyer are tasked with representing Super Earth on the battlefield in the fight for Managed Democracy.

This title truly shines in the nitty gritty details of the gameplay. The movement is smooth and fluid. The controls are intuitive and responsive. The gunplay is immaculate, in my opinion. A plethora of selection available to you, some more powerful guns are ready to be dropped from orbit in the form of stratagem. Weapons function as you would expect. For example, if a round is chambered and you reload your mag, you don't have to cycle the weapon (because there's already a round in there! who woulda thunk?). The impact that rounds have on target is something not just seen, but felt too. You can FEEL the way your bullets eat into the bug's flesh and rip it to shreds. The experience of mowing down a group of hunters with a Stalwart as they advance on your position and attempt to flank you is exhilarating.

Which goes right into my next point, the enemies; anti-democratic SCUM. The lifeless Automatons who mindlessly march towards a pathetic and meaningless life of communist servitude. They wish to see the rest of the galaxy suffer the same fate. The bots are not the only threat to liberty, though. As previously mentioned, the Terminid bug race relentlessly encroaches on our doorstep, aimlessly and thoughtlessly devouring everything in their path. This is the duty of a Helldiver. You must prevent these enemies of liberty from interfering with the life of our citizens and their ability to cast their democratic votes.

Fret not, for you are not alone! You have the full backing of your super destroyer ready to assist you on the ground at a moment's notice. Not only do you have the ordinance capability of the ship's onboard orbital guns, you also have Eagle One, a fixed-wing aircraft ready to wipe clean entire groups of combatants in one fell swoop. She is your guardian angel who valiantly soars through the sky, assisting in any way she can to ensure your mission is complete.

With these tools at your disposal and a group of like-minded freedom fighters, you are well on your way to prove your worth as a coveted agent of Managed Democracy:

A Helldiver.

This is easily one of the most entertaining video games on the market, but the problems are starting to majorly outway the good. For starters, the game is usually fair and balanced in general, but the ways of which you die are egregious. Most games don't have friendly fire for the biggest reason that I type this review. With friendly fire, I get teamkilled about 85% of my games. There is always some guy that shoots like a blind garden gnome, or there is that one guy that always brings the orbital walking barrage against terminids; therefore, effectively killing half of the team. I can complete missions deathless on anything up to difficulty 7 and sometimes 8, but I have to actively avoid my own team in most matches. When I'm not getting teamkilled, a magical charger will spawn right behind me and one-shot me, or I will get ****ed by 30 hunters at once while low on ammo. The game also has a variety of bugs (not terminids), and while most of them are fine, sometimes you will randomly be sent spiraling 6,000 feet into the air and meet Morgan Freeman before falling. You may also be unable to get up at times when getting attacked by melee enemies. Flinch is also busted, and devastators will mow you down without you being able to use a stim or shoot back due to the flinchlocking. Also, if you don't feel like getting killed by your team, solo is beyond unbalanced past difficulty 3. Possible: Yes/ Fun: Hell no.


3rd Edit: This game is continuing to devolve rapidly, and the newest update has made anything above difficulty 6 impossible on the terminid side. Impalers are everywhere and take far too much to kill (one literally survived two airstrikes, gas, and two flamethrower canisters). Bile titan spawns went from fair to literally two bile titans every minute, and one match on difficulty 7 had no less than 18 bile titans. The incendiary breaker was also nerfed, and while I don't personally use it, your random teams on difficulty 6-10 are now nerfed against terminids. Also, heavy devastators somehow feel worst, or they're more common. Either way, the game has gone to the deepest pits of the Shadow Realm, and it's going to take a lot to get it back.
